page.title: Software vs Production Partner for Events
page.description: Compare event platforms and production crews so you can decide which purchase covers tools and which covers run-of-show ownership.
page.h1: Is event software the same as a production partner?
page.definition: Event software is a platform that provides streaming, registration and engagement tools. A production partner is a crew that owns the run of show, rehearses speakers, operates the backup stream and delivers the finished recording.
page.quick_answer: Buy the platform for the technology layer; hire a production partner when you need someone to plan, rehearse and execute the live show so your internal team can focus on content and audience.

sections.h2: What does event software actually include?

blocks.p: Event software provides the technical infrastructure for broadcasting, registration and audience interaction, but it does not operate the show for you.

ul: Streaming engine and ingest points (RTMP, SRT, browser-based)
Registration, ticketing and attendee management
Engagement widgets: polls, Q&A, chat, emoji reactions
Branding controls: stage layouts, lower thirds, virtual backgrounds
Analytics dashboards: concurrent viewers, dwell time, poll responses
Integrations: CRM, marketing automation, calendar, SSO

sections.h2: What does a production partner own that software does not?

blocks.p: A production partner takes operational responsibility for the live experience from planning through post-event delivery.

ul: Run-of-show creation and version control
Speaker briefings, tech checks and full rehearsals
Live show calling, cueing graphics and switching sources
Backup stream monitoring and failover execution
Real-time Q&A moderation and speaker coordination
Edited recording, highlight clips and caption files delivered after the event

sections.h2: How do the cost models differ?

blocks.p: Platform fees are recurring licences tied to capacity or features; production fees are project-based and scale with crew size and event complexity.

head: Purchase
Typical model
What drives the price
rows: Monthly or annual licence per host or attendee tier
Attendee capacity, number of hosts, advanced modules
Crew roles, rehearsal days, hybrid venue days, post-production scope

sections.h2: When do you need both at the same time?

blocks.p: You need both when the event is revenue-critical, hybrid, multi-session or requires a polished broadcast standard that internal staff cannot sustain.

ol: Lock the platform licence early so the production partner can build the run of show on the real environment.
Schedule one full rehearsal on the live platform two to five days before the event.
Assign a single show caller who owns the run of show and a platform operator who manages the backend.
Confirm backup stream ingest and recording paths before the first speaker goes live.
Deliver the edited replay within 24 to 48 hours while audience attention is high.

sections.h2: What staffing does each approach require from your team?

blocks.p: Software-only events rely on internal marketers or coordinators to operate the platform; production partnerships shift operational load to the external crew.

ul: Software-only: one coordinator manages registration, uploads slides, starts the broadcast and monitors chat.
Produced webinar: internal owner approves run of show and speaker list; external producer runs rehearsal, live show and backup stream.
Summit or hybrid conference: internal lead handles agenda and stakeholder sign-off; external team provides show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

sections.h2: How do you evaluate a production partner before signing?

blocks.p: Ask for concrete evidence of run-of-show ownership, backup-stream discipline and post-event delivery speed.

ul: Request a sample run-of-show template they use for events of your size.
Ask how they test and switch to a backup stream during a live failure.
Confirm they deliver edited recordings and clips within 24 to 48 hours.
Verify they have produced on your chosen platform (Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard or similar).
Check that they provide speaker briefs, branded slide templates and lower thirds as standard deliverables.

faq.q: Can I use my existing Zoom Webinars licence with a production partner?
faq.a: Yes. A production partner works on the platform you already own, including Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard, and brings the crew, run of show and backup stream.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for a produced webinar versus a summit?
faq.a: A produced webinar needs three to four weeks from brief to live. A summit or online conference needs six to eight weeks to lock venue AV, platform configuration and speaker rehearsals.

faq.q: Does the production partner handle registration and CRM integration?
faq.a: Registration and CRM setup remain platform tasks. The production partner focuses on live operations: run of show, rehearsals, show calling, backup stream and post-event editing.

faq.q: How many crew members does a hybrid conference require?
faq.a: A hybrid conference typically needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator on site or remote, plus camera operators and an encoder technician at the venue.

faq.q: What deliverables should I expect after the event?
faq.a: Expect a full edited recording, short highlight clips, caption files, run-of-show archive and a brief post-event report with concurrent viewer peaks and engagement metrics.
